input.risks:
1. **New `select` state object on symbols is a real (small) behaviour change.** Today symbols have no `'select'` state, so `elementStateProxy` → `createSelectDefaultState(el, 'select', undefined)` (`src/util/states.ts:280-295`) returns `undefined` and nothing happens on select. After the fix a `select` state exists (even when its style is `{}`), so `createSelectDefaultState` fills in `state.z2 = el.z2 + Z2_SELECT_LIFT` (= 9). Radar symbols are created with `z2: 100` (`RadarView.ts:68`), so selected symbols become `z2: 109`. This is the same behaviour every other symbol-based series already has, and it only affects radar series with `selectedMode` enabled — but it is a visual delta a screenshot test could catch. If you want to avoid it, use Option B and skip assigning the `select` state when `selectItemStyle` has no keys — though that would diverge from `src/chart/helper/Symbol.ts`.

2. **Default blur is preserved, verify it stays that way.** Assigning `state.style = {}` for `blur` must not break the implicit "fade to 10% opacity" behaviour. It does not: `createBlurDefaultState` (`src/util/states.ts:297-324`) checks `blurStyle.opacity == null` and injects `fromState.opacity * 0.1`, so an empty blur style behaves exactly as no blur style. Worth an explicit manual check by hovering a legend item with no `blur` option configured.

3. **Option A calls `getItemStyle()` 3× per symbol per render** (previously 1× per data item). For a radar with many indicators × many series this is a measurable but small increase in model reads. Option B avoids it. Pick B if you care about the render hot path; A if you prefer the codebase-idiomatic one-liner.

4. **`emphasis` semantics must not change.** `setStatesStylesFromModel(symbolPath, itemModel)` resolves emphasis via `itemModel.getModel(['emphasis', 'itemStyle']).getItemStyle()`, which is the same model node as the current `emphasisModel.getModel('itemStyle').getItemStyle()`. Equivalent — but confirm no reviewer expects `emphasisModel` (line 226) to have picked up anything extra, since it is still needed for `focus`/`blurScope`/`disabled` at line 263 and must not be deleted.

5. **No existing unit tests cover this.** `test/ut/spec/` has no radar directory at all (only `api`, `chart/line`, `component`, `data`, `model`, `scale`, `series`, `util`); the sole file under `test/ut/spec/chart/` is `test/ut/spec/chart/line/__tmp_repro.test.ts`, an unrelated leftover scratch file. So nothing under `test/ut/spec` will regress, and nothing there proves the fix. If a regression test is wanted, add `/workspace/test/ut/spec/chart/radar/RadarView.test.ts` using `createChart` from `/workspace/test/ut/core/utHelper.ts` (signature: `createChart({width?, height?, theme?, opts?})`), then assert on `chart.getModel().getSeriesByIndex(0).getData().getItemGraphicEl(0)` → `itemGroup.childAt(2)` is the `symbolGroup`, and `symbolGroup.childAt(0).states.blur.style` / `.states.select.style` reflect the configured `blur.itemStyle` / `select.itemStyle`.

6. **Manual/visual test entries exist but none exercise blur**: `/workspace/test/radar.html`, `/workspace/test/radar2.html`, `/workspace/test/radar3.html`, `/workspace/test/radar4.html`, `/workspace/test/radar-axis.html` — grep for `blur` across them returns nothing. Verifying the fix by eye requires adding `blur: { itemStyle: { ... } }` plus `emphasis: { focus: 'self' }` to one of these; I did not modify any files.
